'''Werner''' is a prominent [[Lunar craters|lunar]] [[impact crater]] that lies in the rugged south-central highlands of the [[Moon]]. It was named after the 15th-century German mathematician and astronomer [[Johannes Werner]].<ref>{{gpn|6523}}</ref> It is almost joined with the crater [[Aliacensis (crater)|Aliacensis]] to the southeast, and the pair form a rugged valley in the intervening gap. Due west of Werner is the distorted [[Regiomontanus (crater)|Regiomontanus]], and to the north is the remains of [[Blanchinus (crater)|Blanchinus]]. It is from the [[Eratosthenian]] period, which lasted from 3.2 to 1.1 billion years ago.<ref>[https://pubs.er.usgs.gov/publication/pp1348 The geologic history of the Moon].  [[USGS]] Professional Paper 1348. By [[Don Wilhelms|Don E. Wilhelms]], John F. McCauley, and Newell J. Trask.  U.S. Government Printing Office, Washington: 1987.  Table 12.2.</ref>

The rim of Werner shows little appearance of wear, and is much younger and less eroded than the other large craters in the surroundings. The interior wall is [[wiktionary:terrace|terrace]]d, and there is a noticeable rampart on the exterior. There are several low rises on the crater floor and a notable central peak. Its highly [[terraced walls]] attain peaks of almost 1,500 feet. The crater is 45 miles (70 kilometers) in diameter, and the difference in height between its rim and its deepest parts is 4.2 kilometers.<ref name="a">''Autostar Suite Astronomer Edition''. CD-ROM. Meade, April 2006.</ref><ref>Moore, Patrick (2001). ''On the Moon''. Sterling Publishing Co.. {{ISBN|0-304-35469-4}}.</ref>

Near the Werner crater, a [[chiaroscuro]] effect created by the dark craters and their lit rims is visible for several hours before first quarter forms an [[Lunar X|X]].
